title: cross-shift-lens-catalog-and-deferred-tasks-2026-07-22
content:
Purpose:
This note summarizes the cross-shift observations, quick triage actions, and deferred tasks for the incoming SRE shift. Goal is to give the next engineer an actionable sandbox of what remains open and which runbook edits are required.

High level summary (TL;DR):
- Two operational anomalies observed across the window (06:00-14:00 UTC): 1) intermittent embedding-service tail latency spikes correlated with kv-cache churn; 2) a Dedicated GPU pool autoscaler flapping that caused short request queuing (~45s) for some model routes. Customer-visible error rate remained low (<0.3%), but several internal retries and elevated token latency were observed.

Incident A — embedding-service tail spikes (detected 2026-07-22 09:12 UTC):
- Signal: sudden increase in p99 for /v1/embeddings endpoint from 120ms -> 1.8s over ~6 minutes. Grafana alert fired (alert id: emb-tail-01).
- Correlated signals: Redis prefix-kv eviction rate increased, cache-hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 37% on the embedding-shard-3 region; continuous-batcher queue depth transiently rose.
- Immediate actions taken:
  - Scaled up embedding pool by one node (manual scale) to increase cache capacity (09:17 UTC).
  - Short-circuit: applied a transient routing rule to route low-priority jobs to cheaper model variant to protect latency for production routes (09:24 UTC).
  - Restarted embedding-service secondary process on node eid-emb-7 to clear excessive local cache thrash (09:30 UTC).
- Observed outcome: latency returned to baseline by 09:40 UTC. No 5xx spike.
- Temporary mitigation: increased kv-cache capacity config for affected pool (temp bump of mem limit +10%).
- What likely happened: bulk cache invalidation due to a job that re-uploaded a large embedding index (probable customer evaluation run) causing hot-key eviction and cold-starts across many pods.
- Open follow-ups (priority: P2):
  - SRE-5021: add a detection rule for sudden cache-hit ratio drops with automated routing fallback (owner: Priya).
  - Engineering: add isolation knob to block index ingestion from affecting production cache (owner: Maya).
  - Runbook delta: add step to check `redis/prefix-eviction` and consider temporary route shift before scaling (see runbook proposal below).

Incident B — Dedicated autoscaler flapping (detected 2026-07-22 11:05 UTC):
- Signal: Dedicated pool autoscaler reported 3 scaling up/scale down cycles in 9 minutes for dedicated-pool-eu-west-2; queue length on gateway increased to ~36 during the flaps.
- Correlated signals: metric `k8s/hpa/desired_replicas` oscillating; cloud provider API returning rate limit warnings for scaling calls.
- Immediate actions taken:
  - Put autoscaler into manual mode for the pool and set target capacity to 6 (11:12 UTC).
  - Cleared pending scale requests in the orchestration queue (11:15 UTC).
  - Opened support ticket with cloud provider for API rate-limit (SRE-5023) (11:18 UTC).
- Observed outcome: queue drained and request latency normalized by 11:30 UTC.
- Root cause hypothesis: noisy external autoscaling config combined with aggressive HPA cool-down settings; provider-side rate-limit exacerbated oscillation.
- Open follow-ups (priority: P1):
  - SRE: formalize safe-mode procedure for autoscaler flapping (owner: Ethan).
  - Infra: introduce aggregate backoff for scaling API calls (owner: Jamal).
  - Runbook delta: add explicit instruction to switch to manual capacity and notify Platform PagerDuty before toggling autoscaler (added below).

Other notes during shift:
- Minor Sentry alerts for `function-router` with increased 429s pinned to an upstream quota; team notified and quota increased (PR 764 linked).
- Weekly maintenance job (analytics/embedding-backfill) started earlier than schedule at 08:50 UTC — ops agreed to reschedule to low-traffic window. Owner: Data Eng (Maya to confirm new cron).

Runbook deltas (proposed edits, please review & commit):
1) embedding-service-runbook.md
  - New step "assess cache-hit ratio" immediately after alert; if ratio <50% for >3min, apply routing fallback before scaling.
  - Add sample Grafana query and threshold values.
  - Add contact: Data Eng on-call (Slack: #data-eng-oncall).
2) dedicated-autoscaler.md
  - Add manual-mode checklist: how to set target replicas, clear orchestration queue, and where to record the manual override.
  - Add troubleshooting flow for cloud API rate limits and backoff knobs.

Action items assigned (with owners):
- Priya: open SRE-5021 detection rule and add unit test for cache delta alert (due 2026-07-25).
- Ethan: draft autoscaler safe-mode runbook snippet (due 2026-07-24).
- Jamal: follow up with infra on provider API rate-limit and propose rate-limit-aware scaling (due 2026-07-26).
- Maya: confirm reschedule of analytics backfill and prevent future out-of-window starts (due 2026-07-23).

Metrics to monitor for next shift (dashboards):
- Grafana: sre/embeddings/p99_latency, sre/embeddings/cache_hit_ratio, redis/prefix-eviction-rate
- Grafana: infra/dedicated/autoscaler/desired_vs_actual_replicas, gateway/queue_length, cloud-api/error_rate
- Sentry: function-router 429 frequency

Notes for incoming engineer (explicit handoff checklist):
1) Check Grafana panels above at start of shift. Note any p99 abnormality.
2) Inspect `redis/prefix-eviction` for embedding-shard-3. If eviction spikes persist, do not immediately scale; apply routing fallback as per proposed runbook and notify Data Eng.
3) Verify dedicated-pool-eu-west-2 autoscaler is in manual mode (it was left manual at 6 replicas) and check cloud provider support ticket SRE-5023 for updates.
4) If queue length > 20 for >5 minutes, escalate to Platform PD and set temporary throttles on non-critical routes.
5) Document any manual override in the shift log and create a follow-up JIRA if not already open.

Post-shift housekeeping:
- I will open SRE-5021 and update the embeddings runbook draft with the Grafana query snippet; PR will be linked in Confluence.
- Tagging today's note for review and incorporation into the weekly on-call retrospective.

Appendix (quick commands & queries):
- Redis eviction check: `redis-cli -h redis-emb-3 INFO | grep eviction`
- Cache-hit query (Grafana/PromQL): `sum(rate(redis_keyspace_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(redis_keyspace_misses_total[5m]))`
- Clear orchestration queue (internal tool): `opsctl queue drain --pool dedicated-pool-eu-west-2 --confirm`

Slack/PD channels: #sre-ops, #sre-incident, PagerDuty: SRE-Pager

Signed-off-by: Priya Rao (on-call)
